_comment: Pinned harness (CLI) and model versions for runs from 2026-09-19.
Dated rather than mutable: the config that produced a set of results stays
readable alongside them. Start a new config_<YYYYMMDD>.json when bumping.
Bumped from config_20260728.json, which pinned claude-code 2.1.81 with
claude-opus-4-6 and codex 0.116.0 with gpt-5.4. Those were the most-used
versions in harbor-jobs at the time, chosen to stay comparable to the published
results. This config is the opposite choice: the newest of each, to measure
current agents on the current benchmark.
gpt-5.6-sol rather than gpt-6-astra. Astra is newer (2026-08-27) and more
capable, but costs $10/$50 per 1M tokens against Sol's $5/$30, over long agentic
sessions across many trials. Sol is the deepest-reasoning tier of the GPT-5.6
family, itself two releases past gpt-5.4. The -codex model variants stop at
gpt-5.3-codex, so the codex arm runs a general model either way, as it already did.
Entries are RUN ARMS, not tools: an agent plus the model it runs. claude and codex
keep those key names because they do double duty as the judge pins -- the judges are
always those two CLIs whichever agent ran the trial. So this bump changes the judging
as well, which is intended: the judges should be current models too. It follows that
process scores from this config are not comparable to those from config_20260728.json.
ONE entry per CLI tool, deliberately: the agent and the judge share /root/.local/bin
inside the trial container, so whichever installs last wins. Separate agent and
judge versions could therefore never be honoured reliably -- and a single field
makes 'agent and judge run the same CLI' true by construction rather than by
remembering to keep two numbers equal.
terminus arms carry NO harness_version, deliberately. terminus-2 is native harbor
code (a tmux loop calling models through LiteLLM), not an installed CLI, so there is
nothing to pin -- its version is the harbor commit. The cluster runs harbor 0.1.45
from the kristin-podman fork while upstream is at 0.23.0, so the terminus arms here
get new MODELS but the same harbor; see todo.md section 3 step 2.
Consumers must treat the field as optional rather than defaulting it to empty, which
would silently unpin a CLI arm. Terminus reaches models via LiteLLM, so it needs
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment (run_harbor.sh --apikeys); the
CLI credential files do not apply.
Consumed at runtime by run_harbor.sh (model via -m, harness via --ak version=)
and by the judge paths (test.sh, rerun_verifier.sh, run_unsupervised_judges.sh)
via tests/versions.json, which is generated from this file.
Two places cannot read it and carry the values literally: each task's
environment/Dockerfile (installs the judge CLIs at image build time) and each
task's tests/versions.json. Do NOT edit those by hand -- edit this file, then:
python harbor-scripts/apply_versions.py           # rewrite all 36
python harbor-scripts/apply_versions.py --check   # report drift, exit 1
NOTE: apply_versions.py and the rerun scripts select the NEWEST config_*.json by
lexical sort, so this file becomes the default as soon as it exists -- before
apply_versions.py has been run. Runs started between the two see a config and
generated files that disagree.
harbor_version pins harbor itself, which for the terminus arms IS the agent version:
terminus-2 is harbor's own code, not an installed CLI, so it has no harness_version to
pin and this field is the only thing that says what ran it. run_harbor.sh reads it to
choose the conda env and the command-line flags, which differ between the two harbors.
0.1.45 cannot run the terminus arms on these models at all -- its terminus sends a
temperature parameter that claude-opus-5 rejects, and every LLM call fails.
max_turns caps a terminus arm's episodes, which terminus-2 otherwise leaves at 1000000.
Measured over the 48 existing terminus trials: the median is 166 steps and terminus-opus
never exceeds 295, but terminus-gpt has a tail at 2006, 2188, 2333, 3196 and 3686 -- runs
that loop rather than work, at 12 to 22 times the median. 800 stops those while leaving
the ambiguous 500-776 band alone. A trial that hits the ceiling is a measurement, not an
infrastructure failure: the agent did not finish, and the cap is recorded here so that is
readable afterwards rather than mysterious. It does not catch a STUCK agent, which makes
no turns at all -- --agent-timeout-multiplier is the backstop for that.
